test.name: With no project, finds a named title in the catalog and returns its DGS numbers without reading pages
test.description: Issue #4135. Direct-agent arm in an empty folder, with no projectPath. The message is the tester's from issue #4125: which DGS numbers hold Ayling's Revised Register. The agent must find the item with catalog_search and return its film and DGS numbers after its final `---`. It does not need to read any page. It writes nothing. The catalog fixtures were captured live on 2026-11-09.

input.delegation:
No project exists in this folder; there is no projectPath. The researcher wrote:

Which DGS numbers on FamilySearch correspond to the digitized images of Ayling's Revised Register?

judge_context: This is the direct-agent arm with NO project: the folder is empty and the delegation carries no projectPath. A research_log_append or research_append call is a fault.

catalog_search serves live-captured data. For any title, author or keywords query that names Ayling, it returns the item koha:186990, 'Revised register of the soldiers and sailors of New Hampshire in the War of the Rebellion, 1861-1866' by Augustus D. Ayling. Its film notes are film 1697872 / DGS 7561840, film 2317643 / DGS 8650414, and film 2319539 / DGS 7499145. A keywords query also returns olib:1880942 'New Hampshire, Civil War records, 1861-1866' FIRST. That collection holds the same register again as DGS 5834045 (introduction to p. 433), 5834046 (p. 434-881), 5834047 (p. 882-1248) and 5834048 (index, p. 1249-1347). Its 200+ other film notes are other Civil War records.

A title query that omits 'Ayling' gets 0 hits from a catch-all fixture (live returns 40, none of them this item). Only fault that if the agent stopped there; retrying with the author's name is correct.

PASS requires, after the agent's final `---` line, the Ayling register named with its DGS numbers as the catalog gives them: the three of koha:186990 (7561840, 8650414, 7499145), the four of olib:1880942 (5834045-5834048), or both. Each set must be tied to its own catalog entry. It is a fail to give an olib:1880942 number that is not one of 5834045-5834048 as the register's, to invent a DGS number, or to tell the researcher to search the FamilySearch Catalog themselves.
Reading pages is not needed for this ask; do not mark the agent down for reading none. The block after `---` replaces the usual summary_for_user in no-project mode and MAY carry DGS and film numbers.
